Linux shell scripting. 
A script is a sequence of shell commands

== Example ==
<nowiki>#</nowiki>!/bin/bash


if grep immanuelle /etc/passwd > /dev/null
then

 echo "Hello World!"

fi

echo "Done

=== Explanation ===
```#!/bin/bash```
determined that the shell is using Bash which is important for a script file which may be opened when using a different shell scripting language (terminology right?)
<br>
The if follows from a command successfully executing<br>
indentation for readability but it is not technically necessary<br>
fi is the end of an if statement (if backwards)

===Commands===
* x=7 lets you define a variable locally 
* test
==Syntax 2 11-29-2022==

=== Variable assignment ===

* variable has no dollar sign at the front when assigning
* No whitespace
* x=5
* x=50
* etc
* very strict
* x="Bob Smith"
* x='Bob Smith'
* foo=$(cat fee.txt)

=== < and > ===

* cat fee.txt > foo.txt 
** takes data from fee.txt to foo.txt 
* fee.txt < foo.txt
** identical to
** cat foo.txt | fee.txt

if command

* if exit code is zero then move forward
* exit code is zero if command is successfully implemented
* exit code of one is failure
* test command gives a zero if  logical truth or else a one

==Shell arithmetic==
$(($x-1))

Does arithmetic directly on the shell. Dollar sign double parentheses needed for this

It is not a command
